answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks whose results are checked by randomly assigned, stake-bearing reviewers; a reviewer who approves a provably faulty result loses part of its deposit. Because identities alone grant no weight, an attacker must fund many accounts and keep them active, then risk those deposits across tasks and reviews. Splitting one identity into a summit of aliases does not multiply trust: each alias needs separate capital, while colluding reviewers can expose one another to penalties. Even a timber or ember delivery must clear the same checks.
